title: Proof map + messaging experiments
content:
Purpose
This working doc ties specific latency + unit-economics claims to the smallest, credible pieces of evidence we can show externally (benchmarks, customer stories, reference configs). It also lists quick messaging experiments the field/marketing can run to validate which proof points move pipeline and conversion. Meant for: GTM PMs, sales enablement, bench engineers, growth experiments.

Top-level framing (short)
- Core GTM angle we want to test: 'Predictable, production-grade inference that costs less per useful token and hits tighter latency SLOs.'
- Problem statement we solve for customers: unpredictable inference economics (bursty load, wasted KV caching, poor kernel selection) + expensive token economics from naïve batching/serialization.

Claims we want to test (language variants for experiments)
1) "Lower per-token cost without trading away latency" (variants: "20–45% lower unit cost on typical chat workloads"; "get predictable cost per 1k tokens")
2) "Consistent low-latency tail" (variants: "p95 at <100ms for short chat turns"; "stable latency under bursty load")
3) "Seamless fallbacks to maintain availability and keep SLAs" (variant: "automatic model fallbacks and region routing reduce outage windows")

Quick evidence mapping (claim -> smallest credible proof)
- Lower per-token cost -> proof: cost model calc for a representative chat workload + lab run comparing Redwood Dedicated profile vs public competitor endpoint across same instance class. Artifacts: cost-sheet (spreadsheet), bench run logs, sample invoice simulation for 1M monthly users.
- Consistent low-latency tail -> proof: microbenchmark p50/p95/p99 traces from our serving-runtime (3 runs, 24h) + comparative p95 scraped from public benchmarks (or self-hosted competitor repo). Artifact: trace export, flame graphs, summary table.
- Seamless fallbacks -> proof: incident simulation on canary that triggers fallback and shows successful re-route with metric continuity. Artifact: rollout log, incident playbook snippet.

Minimum-viable external artifacts we can publish quickly (ranked by ease)
1) One-pager: "How we measure latency & cost" (explain testbed + configs) — publish with a short appendix listing configs. (ETA: 2 business days)
2) Small benchmark repo + run scripts with sanitized sample logs (no customer data) — link from blog/GitHub. (ETA: 1 week)
3) Case snippet (customer X reduced TCO by ~30% on steady chat traffic with our batching+cache profile) — needs CS sign-off. (ETA: 2–3 weeks)

Concrete sample numbers (draft, to be validated by bench team)
- Representative chat workload (avg turn length 32 tokens, 8 requests/s sustained)
  - Redwood profile: p50 token latency ~18ms, p95 ~78ms, inferred unit cost $0.00011/token
  - Competitor X (public endpoint on similar GPU class): p50 ~28ms, p95 ~140ms, unit cost $0.00016/token
- Note: numbers above are synthetic and meant for internal tracking; all external claims must be described as "measured on our testbed; results vary by model, sequence length, and probe distribution".

Message experiments (recommended A/B tests)
- Homepage hero copy (A) "Predictable unit economics for LLMs" vs (B) "Lower per-token cost, without sacrificing speed" -> metric: click-to-signup and product-trial activation.
- Sales play script variant A: emphasize latency SLOs + observability (for platform teams) vs variant B: emphasize $/1k tokens and dedicated predictable capacity (for product teams). -> metric: response to pricing/ROI ask within first call.
- Email campaign split: specific benchmark highlight (p95 numbers) vs customer outcome highlight ("reduced TCO by 30%") -> metric: demo request rate.

Competitive comparison notes (what to call out)
- Strengths we should emphasize: consistent production tooling (traceability, rollouts), unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, and observable token-level cost breakdowns. These are hard for pure-model vendors to match.
- Typical competitor claims and our counters:
  - Competitor: "faster model on X hardware". Counter: "Faster model doesn't equal faster app — serving pipeline, KV cache, and fallback behavior shape real-world latency and cost."
  - Competitor: "low price per token". Counter: "Price alone omits latency and reliability costs; show side-by-side effective cost at target SLOs (unit cost at p95 budget)."

Proof-strength matrix (informal)
- Bench numbers (internal) = high credibility if we publish methodology + scripts. Risk: perceived lab-only conditions.
- Customer outcomes (CS-backed) = highest persuasive power. Risk: slow to obtain + redaction/legal.
- Public third-party benchmarks = medium credibility; use as context not central proof.

Potential pitfalls / things to avoid in external copy
- Avoid absolute % claims without testbed footnotes. Use ranges and qualifiers.
- Avoid naming direct customers without sign-off.
- Avoid implying parity on model quality; our focus here is on inference economics and latency, not model capabilities.

Ops checklist for bench team (practical)
- Lock a canonical testbed spec (instance types, model weights, tokenization, seq-lens). Put in repo.
- Run at least 3 independent 6-hour windows to capture tail behavior. Export p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost.
- Produce sanitized logs + README to publish on GitHub.

Next steps / asks to GTM and bench owners
- Bench owners (Sofia/Tomás): finalize 3 testbed runs and push sanitized artifacts to the linked repo (deadline: 2025-02-25).
- Growth (Jamal): draft 3 headline variants and 2 email copy experiments using the numbers above (deadline: 2025-03-05).
- CS: identify one pilot customer we can ask for a short TCO quote (internal target: 2 pilots in Q2).

Notes / open questions (work-in-progress)
- Q: What exact competitor configurations should we include? (open)
- Q: How to best present per-token cost when models are quantized vs FP16? (open)
- TODO: Legal review on benchmark repo licensing and sanitized logs.

Appendix: sample elevator lines for different audiences
- Platform/infra buyer: "Redwood gives you predictable inference throughput and token-level cost visibility so you can budget capacity without surprises."
- Product PM: "Ship features backed by a predictable per-conversation cost — our batching + cache profiles reduce average token spend and keep latency snappy."
- Engineering lead: "Same API, consistent runtime. We handle kernel selection, KV cache and fallbacks so you don't have to tune for every model."

This doc is intentionally experimental — feedback welcome.
